summary: All stage-2c semantic checks passed. The implementation computes predicted-label final-layer gradient embeddings and performs seeded incremental k-MEANS++ selection over those embeddings.

checks_summary.note: All annotated BADGE elements are implemented on the live select_batch path with penultimate activations, predicted labels, and gradient-space sampling.
The same gradient-embedding and k-MEANS++ logic runs at demo and paper scale; the pool-size clamp does not replace algorithmic behavior.
The only smoke-pool accommodation, clamping an oversized request to available candidates, is explicitly marked paper-fidelity.
select_batch calls the hallucinated-gradient computation followed by k-MEANS++ rather than a score-ranking or random fallback.
A local generator constructed from seed supplies both the uniform first-center draw and every subsequent weighted draw.
The sampler retains and updates one nearest-squared-distance vector, without all-center tensor materialization.
select_batch neither mutates the pool nor stores acquisition state and returns pool-relative indices from its supplied tensor.
Not applicable: BADGE has no Stage-1 core-set constructor; its declared initialization is the notebook-owned random labeled bootstrap.
No scalar ranking claim is made; subsequent centers are sampled from the correctly squared nearest-distance distribution.
Both core methodology elements are preserved: real penultimate predicted-label gradient blocks and seeded k-MEANS++ over those blocks.
The live embedding path constructs the output-layer cross-entropy gradient under the argmax hypothetical label.
argmax over logits is equivalent to argmax over the paper's softmax probabilities.
Softmax probabilities feed the exact cross-entropy derivative represented by the residual vector; explicit loss evaluation is unnecessary for this closed-form gradient.
residuals.unsqueeze(-1) multiplied by embedding.unsqueeze(1) implements each (p_i - I(y_hat=i))z block before flattening.
The maintained vector is the squared Euclidean distance to the nearest selected center, updated by elementwise minimum.
Sampling normalizes squared nearest-center distances, with selected positions zeroed to preserve unique centers.

caveats: The implementation uses the closed-form softmax cross-entropy derivative rather than constructing the scalar loss and differentiating it; this is mathematically equivalent to Equation (1).
